title: Stelo SPARK Study: Behavioral and Glycemic Effects of Glucose Visibility
official: Stelo SPARK Study: Behavioral and Glycemic Effects of Glucose Visibility - Software Multi-Session Usability Study
summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the impact of glucose visibility provided by the Stelo Glucose Biosensor System on participants' glucose insight, decision confidence, self-regulation, and health-related behaviors. The study enrolls US-based adults (≥18 years) across four groups: individuals with type 2 diabetes not treated with insulin, individuals with prediabetes, individuals in perimenopause, and healthy-living individuals. Participants complete baseline assessments and a blinded Stelo wear period, followed by \~30 days of unblinded Stelo use across two consecutive wear periods. Behavioral, psychosocial, and glycemic outcomes are assessed through periodic patient-reported outcome (PRO) surveys and semi-structured interviews collected at baseline, 15 days, and 30 days. The primary outcome is change in perceived glucose insight and decision confidence.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Participants may be included if they meet all of the following criteria:

* Ages ≥ 18 years (at the time of the Screening Visit)
* Willing to wear the Systems for the total duration of study wear per session
* Willing to comply with all study-session specific instructions and procedures
* Able to speak, read, and write English

Exclusion Criteria:

Participants will be excluded if they meet any of the following criteria during active study session participation:

* Presence of extensive skin changes/diseases at sensor wear site(s) that preclude wearing the sensor(s) on skin (e.g., extensive psoriasis, recent burns or severe sunburn, extensive eczema, extensive scarring, extensive tattoos, or dermatitis herpetiformis)
* Known severe allergy to medical-grade adhesives
* Required or scheduled to have a Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scan, Computed Tomography (CT) scan, or diathermy
* Currently using Hydroxyurea for treatment
* Any condition or current treatment (medication) that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would interfere with their participation in the study session, use of the device or pose excessive risk to study staff. Some examples of conditions that Investigators may consider exclusionary are HIV, Hepatitis B, or Hepatitis C infections; active illegal substance use; or active psychiatric disorder.
* Work for a Pharmaceutical or medical equipment manufacturer, Market research or advertising firm , or Public relations firm.
